headline: A US court case over who owns the AI-made meme character Tung Tung Tung Sahur could help decide whether AI-generated art can be copyrighted.
score_reason: Pool score kept; interesting legal test case, but no ruling yet.
importance_line: Creators of AI-assisted characters and the businesses that license them are affected; the case may set an early precedent, but the court has not ruled and the outcome is unknown.
summary: The Guardian reports that two companies behind the Roblox game "Steal a Brainrot" are suing French agency Mementum, which represents the Indonesian teen who made the meme character Tung Tung Tung Sahur with OpenAI's image tool, arguing that the character cannot be copyrighted because AI-generated work lacks a human author. Mementum has pursued a takedown under EU law and a US trademark claim instead, and the Guardian quotes a Cornell law professor saying the case could show what counts as copyrightable when AI is involved.
